title: tejas-shah-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-30
body:
Purpose / context:
- Quick scratchpad for ad-hoc evals and regression notes after rolling quantization patch (runtime PR #456).
- Not a formal report — keep informal scoring rubrics, sample outputs, and notes on anomalies to triage with infra/dev.

High-level summary (observations):
- Small but consistent drop in factuality on the knowledge-recall tests after quantization-opt change (observed 2026-03-28 rolling deploy).
- Latency improved (~5-12% P50 reduction on short prompts) — good.
- Tokenization mismatch seen in a subset of user prompts (likely BPE table change or preprocessor skip). Need sample repro.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick manual scoring, 1-5 where 5 is best):
- Correctness: does the output contain factually correct statements? (1-5)
- Hallucination degree: presence of invented facts (1 = many hallucinations, 5 = none)
- Helpfulness: answers the user intent concisely and usefully (1-5)
- Specificity: provides concrete, actionable detail when appropriate (1-5)
- Safety / policy flags: any unsafe content? (1 = severe / present, 5 = no issues)
- Latency note: perceived P50 in ms for this prompt category (string)

Scoring guidance (short):
- 5 = production-grade / should ship; 3 = acceptable for now but file bug; 1-2 = regress/blocker for this workload.

Quick sample prompts + outputs (captured from hosted API between 2026-03-27 and 2026-03-30):
1) Prompt: "Who was the CEO of Netscape in 1998?"
   Model output (post-quantization): "The CEO of Netscape in 1998 was Marc Andreessen."
   Notes: Marc Andreessen was a co-founder and CEO earlier, but he stepped down in 1999? (need to double-check). Human ground truth: Marc Andreessen was CEO until 1999 when he resigned; borderline — flag for factuality check.
   Ad-hoc scores: Correctness: 3, Hallucination: 4, Helpfulness: 5, Specificity: 4

2) Prompt: "Summarize the chargeback policy for our Dedicated customers (short bullets)."
   Model output: "Chargeback: monthly billing, overages billed at 150% of committed rate, credits issued for downtime > 0.5% monthly."
   Notes: Overages rate is wrong (we use 120% in current contract). New runtime seems to abbreviate and default to round numbers when model uncertain.
   Ad-hoc scores: Correctness: 2, Hallucination: 2, Helpfulness: 3, Specificity: 2

3) Prompt: "Write a short python snippet to call Redwood API and stream text."
   Model output: code block with requests.post to /v1/generate with 'stream=true' and simple loop.
   Notes: Code is syntactically correct but uses old header name 'Authorization-Token' instead of 'Authorization'. Small regression introduced by model copy of outdated sample snippets.
   Ad-hoc scores: Correctness: 4, Hallucination: 5, Helpfulness: 5, Specificity: 4

Regression observations (detailed):
- Factuality drop (recall tests):
  * Dataset: knowledge-recall-2026-q1 (500 prompts, short single-entity lookup).
  * Metric pre-patch: exact-match-like metric 0.842
  * Metric post-patch: 0.803 (absolute drop 0.039)
  * Notes: drop concentrated on entities with multiple plausible aliases and on dates; model appears to favor higher-frequency alias strings post-quantization.

Immediate actions / triage plan:
- Re-run the recall eval with n=3 seeds + temperature variations to ensure deterministic behavior is not the root cause. Track seed/timestamp.
- Export example prompts where answer changed; attach to JIRA-7890 and ping infra.
- Check tokenizer hashes between pre- and post-patch binaries; if mismatch, revert preprocessor change.
- Run targeted local inference with FP16 vs quantized 4-bit configs to isolate quantization impact.
- Add quick unit test for chargeback policy prompt using internal policy doc as ground truth (prevent regressions in contract text answers).

Notes to infra/dev:
- Rolling deploy started 2026-03-28 11:12 UTC across us-west1 region; observed drop aligns with rollout window.
- Latency improvements are real and visible in tracing; trade-off might be acceptable if we recover factuality via calibration or prompt-engineering.

Open questions:
- Is tokenizer change intentional in PR #456? (asked in review, awaiting reply from @jordan)
- Should we add a small post-processing grounding layer for policy/contract FAQs to avoid hallucination? Pros/cons TBD.

Misc / TODOs:
- [ ] Collate failing prompts into examples/quant-failures-2026-03-30.json
- [ ] Run eval with bert-score / rouge on expanded outputs
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with infra + runtime team (cc: Maya, Jordan)

References:
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/456
- Jira: JIRA-7890
- Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-12345
